title: NASA satellite data shows 2026 El Niño event
excerpt: Altimetry satellites indicate the current El Niño pattern resembles the 1997 event.
bodyHtml:
NASA reported on October 23, 2026, that satellite altimetry data shows sea levels are higher than normal across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. This pattern is a hallmark of the El Niño climate phenomenon, which involves warmer-than-normal water in the equatorial Pacific.

Data from the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite indicates that the 2026 event is similar in character to the 1997-98 El Niño. According to Josh Willis, a project scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the current event is on track to be even bigger than the 1997 event.

The 2015-16 El Niño was also very strong, but its pattern differed from those in October 1997 and October 2026. NOAA’s October 8, 2026, outlook predicted an 83 percent chance of a strong-to-very strong El Niño through the first three months of 2027.
